clue.text: I gain one second to come first

indicators.note: says the letters for one and second are placed ahead of the word for gain

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
S is the standard abbreviation for a second of time
to land something, such as a job or a prize, is to gain it

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that by gaining a single second they will finish the race in first place.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening I is not a pronoun but the definition, the map abbreviation. 'to come first' puts I and S ahead of LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: On maps and in reference books the abbreviation I stands for a piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Hold good area for spectators put up with principled position

definitions.meaning: to remain valid, as an offer or a rule continues in force
the covered seating at a sports ground
a firm stance taken on an issue

explanation.surface: Someone explains that seating for fans should be retained because it reflects a stance on principle.
explanation.definitionFit: Four senses of one word: to remain valid, a grandstand, to tolerate, and a firm stance taken on a matter.

clue.text: Tipsy pirate providing drink

indicators.note: a drunk person's steps lurch about, so the letters of pirate stagger into a new order

parts.note: providing, as in 'providing that', means if

explanation.surface: A drunken buccaneer is offered something more to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipsy' looks like it describes the pirate, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Industry fabricating ceiling and walls to decorate

indicators.note: making something up, so the letters of ceiling are put together afresh
the walls of a word are its outside letters, here the ends of decorate, which enclose the rest

explanation.surface: A decorator works hard building a ceiling and walls ready for painting.
explanation.walkthrough: The walls of a word are its outer letters; 'fabricating' then shuffles them in with the letters of the ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry in the sense of hard-working application is a synonym of steady, careful effort.

clue.text: Prickly character initially chafing at casual treatment by you and me

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the four words that follow it

parts.note: you and me together are us

explanation.surface: A touchy person bristles at being treated off-handedly by the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' covers four words, chafing, at, casual and treatment, giving CACT.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiny desert plant is literally a prickly thing; 'character' plays on a touchy personality.

clue.text: Song is something sung by gondolier when stripping naked

indicators.note: stripping off removes the letters of the word for naked from the song

parts.note: a barcarole is the traditional boating song of Venetian gondoliers
naked means bare

explanation.surface: A Venetian boatman sings his song while undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when stripping' removes B, A, R and E, scattered in order through the gondolier's song, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol is a joyful song, most often a Christmas hymn.

clue.text: Shared ground, almost one side of cricket pitch

indicators.note: almost the whole thing, so the final letter of the punctuation mark's name is lost

parts.note: the punctuation mark printed after the definition is itself a comma, used here as a word
on, or the leg side, is one of the two halves of a cricket field

explanation.surface: Land used by everyone, almost half a cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed comma is part of the wordplay: 'almost' cuts its name to COMM. ON is the leg side, the half of a cricket field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A village green open to all residents is a tract of land held in shared use.

clue.text: Forcibly removing criminal into unorthodox group's housing

indicators.note: one set of letters gives a home to the other, enclosing it
unconventional, so the letters of group depart from their usual order
crooked, so the letters of into are bent out of shape

explanation.surface: A crook is taken in and sheltered by a band of eccentrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' gives UPROG and 'criminal' gives OTIN, the two scrambles; 'housing' looks like accommodation but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprooting means pulling something out by the roots, so forcibly dislodging or removing it.

clue.text: Shell-like bone in middle of fossil record

indicators.note: the recording sits inside the central letters
takes the central pair of letters of the word fossil

parts.note: a tape is a recording

explanation.surface: A shell-shaped bone appears halfway through the fossil record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell-like' is crossword slang for the ear, not a description of shape; 'middle of' and 'in' are the selection and container signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The stirrup bone is the smallest bone of the middle ear, and shell-like is a jokey term for the ear.

clue.text: Evergreen tree hampering attempt to climb

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters are read from bottom to top
getting in the way, so the word for attempt sits in the middle of the tree

parts.note: the elm is a common tree
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: A tree hinders someone's efforts to scale it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hampering' builds ELTRYM; in a down clue 'to climb' reads it from the bottom up. 'Evergreen' alone is the definition, though 'Evergreen tree' looks like one.
explanation.definitionFit: The myrtle is an aromatic shrub that keeps its glossy leaves all year round.

clue.text: Itinerant artist against being framed by informant

indicators.note: the pieces for artist and against are surrounded by the word for informant

parts.note: a teller is one who tells, so an informant
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: A wandering painter protests at being set up by a grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being framed by' suggests a stitch-up but means enclosed; 'grass' in the surface is British slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerant as a noun is a person who travels from place to place, a wanderer.

clue.text: Tipsy Lord admits blunder

indicators.note: lets in, so the word for blunder goes inside the exclamation

parts.note: 'My!' and 'Lord!' are both exclamations of surprise
to blunder is to err

explanation.surface: A drunken peer confesses to a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord' looks like a peer, but it is the exclamation 'My!'
explanation.definitionFit: Merry is a mild euphemism for slightly drunk, as after a few drinks.

clue.text: One course of half-eaten meal swimming in fat left unfinished

indicators.note: the remains of the meal float inside the shortened word for fat
the last letter of the word for fat is dropped

parts.note: pudgy means plump or fat

indicators.note: only the first half of the word for meal remains

parts.note: dinner is a meal

explanation.surface: A greasy meal, partly eaten, is left floating in fat.
explanation.walkthrough: Both shortenings act on synonyms, not on clue words: 'half-eaten' leaves the first half of the meal, 'left unfinished' docks the last letter of the word for fat, and 'swimming in' sets one in the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudding is the sweet course of a British meal, also called dessert.

clue.text: Watch thug circling round floor

indicators.note: surrounding, so the word for thug goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a lout is a rough, aggressive man
O is round in shape
to floor an opponent is to knock them out, KO

explanation.surface: Watch a heavy go round and knock someone to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is not a container signal here but the letter O; 'circling' does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping watch means keeping a careful eye out for danger, the job of a sentry.

clue.text: Reporter's not changing paper?

indicators.note: what a reporter says is spoken, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: stationary means not moving or changing

explanation.surface: A journalist wonders whether a newspaper is failing to move with the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' looks like the reporter's newspaper but means writing materials.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationery covers writing materials such as letter paper and envelopes.

clue.text: Dogmatic author's raising good point about rule of law

indicators.note: in a down clue the author's words lift the rest above them, so they come last
around, so the word for good point surrounds the rule letter

parts.note: an asset is a valuable quality or strength
R is an abbreviation for rule
the setter speaking as author says 'I have', contracted to I've

explanation.surface: A writer pushes a strong point about the rule of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R in ASSET; 'raising' has I'VE hold that up from below in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Assertive means forthright and insistent in stating opinions, close to opinionated or dogmatic.

clue.text: Impervious to irony tainting start of record by reformed Four Tops

indicators.note: places the first letter next to the rest
takes the opening letter of record
a band that has reformed has got back together, so these letters are re-formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A reunited Motown group's comeback record is free of any taint of irony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irony tainting' means corrosion of iron, not sarcasm. The Four Tops were a 1960s Motown vocal group.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that resists corrosion cannot be spoilt by oxidation of its iron, hence the irony pun.

clue.text: In the main, movement is restricted to those attending

indicators.note: those attending a talk are the listeners, so this is what they hear

parts.note: tied means bound or restricted

explanation.surface: Mostly, a political campaign is limited to its participants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly', but the main is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic name for the open sea, whose regular rise and fall is its movement.

clue.text: Patient rushed to occupy lavatory after I left

indicators.note: the word for rushed fills the space inside the shortened lavatory
the letter I departs from the word for lavatory

parts.note: a toilet is a lavatory
rushed means ran

explanation.surface: Someone dashes into the loo once the speaker has come out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after I left' removes the letter I, leaving TOLET; 'to occupy' then fills it.
explanation.definitionFit: Patient and tolerant both describe someone able to bear delays or annoyance without complaint.

clue.text: Plant having no proper flower

indicators.note: the word for proper is taken off the plant

parts.note: the primrose is a spring plant
prim means prudishly proper

explanation.surface: A specimen that doesn't produce a real bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' wants to be the definition, but it is the primrose; 'having no' removes PRIM.
explanation.definitionFit: The rose is the classic garden bloom, a flower in the most literal sense.

clue.text: Withdraw decree requiring revision

indicators.note: a text needing revision must be reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An official order is withdrawn because it needs rewriting.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to move back or retreat, as tides and hairlines do.

clue.text: Reporter's son grew upset with men

indicators.note: knocked over, so the letters of the fodder are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A journalist's boy became annoyed with the men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges SONGREW and MEN together.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsmonger is a gossip who spreads news, a disparaging term for someone who reports it.

clue.text: Chubby Checker's last hit leads to other dancers using new twist

indicators.note: a twist turns things around, so the collected letters are rearranged
takes the final letters of the words for Checker and hit
takes the opening letters of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: Chubby Checker's last hit leads other dancers to adopt a new twist.
explanation.walkthrough: Chubby Checker was the American singer of 'The Twist'. 'last' gives R and T; 'leads to' gives ODUN; 'twist' rearranges all six.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotund means plump and round in figure, a polite synonym of fat.

clue.text: Make a pretence of wager Irishman's accepted

indicators.note: taken in, so the word for wager sits inside the name

parts.note: Pat, short for Patrick, is the stock crossword Irishman
to lay a bet is to wager

explanation.surface: An Irishman takes on a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat is the stock Irishman of crosswords; the 's in 'Irishman's' stands for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: To play at something is to do it half-heartedly, merely going through the motions.

clue.text: County's eastern region briefly brought back old legislation

indicators.note: the eastern end of a word written across is its last few letters, the only part that changes
brought back means turned the other way, so that end stretch is read in reverse
the last letter of the county is dropped, cutting it short

parts.note: Cornwall is the county at the south-western tip of England

explanation.surface: The east of a county once restored ancient laws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts CORNWALL to CORNWAL; 'brought back' reverses only its eastern region, WAL, giving LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: The Corn Laws were 19th-century British tariffs on imported grain, repealed in 1846.

clue.text: The West Indies supply wine

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: WI is the abbreviation for the West Indies, as on cricket scorecards

explanation.surface: The Caribbean islands provide wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is read as 'in a supple way', bending THE and WI into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: White is short for white wine, made from pale grapes or without the skins.

clue.text: Quietly object to offer

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to object to something is to resent it

explanation.surface: Silently protest at a proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to hold it out or put it forward, as a formal gift or proposal.

clue.text: Former French island for Napoleon?

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
île is the French word for island

explanation.surface: An island off France that once belonged to Napoleon.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon was banished to Elba and then St Helena, so a former island was his banishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Banishment to a remote island was Napoleon's fate, twice over.

clue.text: Plant raised area close to conservatory

parts.note: a dais is a raised platform

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A specimen grown on a platform near the glasshouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The common white-petalled lawn flower is a small plant of the aster family.

clue.text: Quarantine breach losing six lives to begin with

indicators.note: places the word for lives at the front

parts.note: lives means exists, is

indicators.note: the Roman six is taken off the word for breach

parts.note: a breach of a rule is a violation
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A breach of quarantine costs six lives at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes VI from VIOLATION, leaving OLATION; 'to begin with' puts IS first.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarantine is enforced separation from others to stop the spread of disease.

clue.text: Insect larvae drawn by source of sugar

indicators.note: places the gutted larvae beside the root crop

parts.note: sugar beet is a source of sugar

indicators.note: a drawn fowl has had its insides taken out, so only the outer letters of larvae remain

explanation.surface: Insect grubs are attracted by something sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' looks like 'attracted' but means disembowelled, leaving LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetles form the largest order of insects, with hard wing cases.

clue.text: PA seems more distant on the phone

indicators.note: a phone carries only the voice, so this is how the word sounds

parts.note: farther means further away

explanation.surface: Dad sounds further away over a telephone line.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the R in the word for more distant is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Pa is a familiar name for one's dad.
